IF YOU WANT TO PASS SYSTEM DESIGN INTERVIEWS, STOP LISTING TECHNOLOGIES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 MOVES:

Start with requirements, not Kafka.

Users, scale, latency. Numbers first. The interviewer wants your thinking, not your stack.

Draw the happy path, then break it.

One box diagram, then ask what dies first. Bottlenecks earn more points than buzzwords.

Always close with tradeoffs.

Why this over that, and what breaks at 10x. Seniors choose and defend.

I post daily breakdowns like this for backend, SQL, and interviews.

Follow @owlsky17 so you don't miss the next one.

IF YOU WANT BEHAVIORAL ROUNDS TO REMEMBER YOU, STOP RECITING YOUR RESUME.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 STORY RULES:

One story per question, 90 seconds max.

Situation, action, result. Rambling loses the room before the result lands.

Lead with the conflict.

What was hard, who disagreed, what was at stake. Tension is what makes stories stick.

End with what you would repeat.

The lesson proves growth. Anyone can survive a mess; seniors extract the rule.

THINGS HIRING MANAGERS CAN'T TELL FROM YOUR RESUME (SO PROVE THEM IN THE INTERVIEW):

How you debug when prod is on fire.

Walk through logs, metrics, and your first three commands. Process beats claims.

Whether you unblock others.

One story about the runbook you wrote or the junior you mentored beats five teamwork bullets.

Whether your numbers are real.

p95 800ms to 480ms with one index, verified over two weeks. Specifics get interviews.
